summary: Jules Bloch was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the EPHE, INALCO, and the University of Paris under Meillet, Lévi, and Foucher. He taught at EPHE (1919–1951), INALCO (1921–1937), and the Collège de France (1936–1951).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Jules Brooks Levinson completed his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, also studying under traditional teachers. He founded the Light of Berotsana Translation Group and taught at Hamline University in 1996.

Jules Luquiens was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Geneva and Yale University under William Dwight Whitney. He served as Professor of French at MIT (1875–1892) and Professor of Modern Languages at Yale (1892–1899).

Linguist Jules Marouzeau studied at the Sorbonne under Antoine Meillet, as well as at the EPHE and Collège de France. He served as Directeur d’études at the EPHE (1920) and Professor of Latin at the Sorbonne (1925–1948).

Historian Jules Michelet studied at Lycée Charlemagne. During his career, he held positions at the École Normale Supérieure, served as a section chief at the Archives nationales (1830–1851), and was Professor of History at the Collège de France (1838–1852).

Jules Oppert worked in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Indology, studying at Heidelberg, Bonn (under Lassen and Freytag), Berlin, and Kiel. He held professorships at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, INALCO, and the Collège de France (1874–1905).

Jules Pierre Barthoux was a scholar of archaeology, history, and Iranian/Central Asian studies who earned a Dr.-ès-sciences from the University of Lille. He was in charge of the Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan from 1923 to 1933.
Jules Thonnelier worked in the fields of Indology and religious studies. His career included memberships in the Société Asiatique (~1855–1879) and the Société de l'histoire de France.

Julia A. B. Hegewald is an Indologist and architectural historian who earned her BA and PhD at SOAS University of London, an MA at the University of Oxford, and completed her Habilitation at RWTH Aachen University.

Julia Ching was a scholar of sinology, philosophy, and religious studies who earned degrees from the College of New Rochelle, Catholic University of America, and Australian National University. She was appointed Professor of Religion, Philosophy, and East Asian Studies at Toronto (1978).

Julia F. Andrews works in the fields of sinology and art history. She completed her studies at Brown University, the University of California, Berkeley, and Harvard University, and joined the faculty at Ohio State University around 1987.

Julia König works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Jena from 2006 to 2013, where she also held a position in the Faculty of Social and Behavioural Sciences from 2008 to 2009.

Julia Leslie was an Indologist and scholar of religion who studied at the University of Sussex and the University of Oxford. Her academic career included serving as Lecturer and Reader in Hindu Studies at SOAS University of London (1990–2004).

Julian Schott is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. His academic posts include being a faculty member at the University of Vienna and a Research Fellow at the University of Hamburg (both attested 2026).

Juliane Schober is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1989. She served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Arizona State University (attested 1997, 2007).

Julie Gifford is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed her Ph.D. at the University of Chicago under the supervision of Frank E. Reynolds. She held an academic post at Miami University (attested 2011).

Julien Girard de Rialle worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied under Honoré-Joseph Chavée and at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes, and later served as a lecturer at the Sorbonne.

Julien Levesque is an Indologist and historian who earned his PhD from EHESS. He has held positions at EHESS, Centre de Sciences Humaines, Ashoka University, the University of Zurich, and as a Research Fellow at the CNRS in 2025.
Julien Vinson was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the École Nationale du Génie Rural, des Eaux et des Forêts. From 1879 to 1921, he served as Professor of Hindustani and Tamil at INALCO.

Julieta Rotaru is an Indologist and linguist who earned degrees from the University of Bucharest and Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth. She has held posts at the University of Bucharest, Södertörn University, and INALCO (2021).
